Also the final year that O-Pee-Chee used this type of card stock that they had used for so many years; the next year bringing in the much more bleached white card backs. WaroftheGods	

My first pack of hockey cards ever opened was 1990-91 O-Pee-Chee. My dad bought me a few packs that day if I remember correctly and as an 8 year old boy I would of rather had candy. I remember that changing as I opened those packs, 2 cards in particular, I pulled a card with my favourite goalie Kelly Headey on it,and those same few packs I also pulled a Gretzky card, dad took the opportunity to teach me the potential values of hockey cards and went back to the store and bought some penny sleeves for my new cards. Who doesn't remember the cards in the early 90's being projected as an investment that will let you retire early lol We all couldn't have been more wrong.

So, I’d like to give my opinion and express my anger about the recent prices of these hockey card boxes. For example, I saw this one: (1990-91 O-Pee-Chee OPC Premier Hockey Box BBCE Wrapped - 36 Packs - Possible JAGR = US $1,151.28). I feel like saying, “What the heck?!” Honestly, it’s outrageous! Over $1,151.28 knowing that, at best, you might pull a Jagr card, for instance. But even then, you’ll need to get it graded or evaluated if you prefer, and there’s absolutely no guarantee you’ll be able to sell it.

First off, there’s no certainty you’ll recoup your $1,151.28 investment. This box is absolutely not worth its price. And the same goes for other boxes like Topps from ‘85/’86/’87/’88/’89. Sure, it’s nice to sell card boxes for over $1,000/$2,000/$3,000, but most of the cards you pull are worthless. And even worse, when you do find a rare one that’s worth something, there’s no guarantee it will sell.

What I’m trying to say is: a box priced at $800 is outrageous. It should be more like $150 at most—that would already be more reasonable. Honestly, I think these people are killing the passion for collecting sports cards. So many young people are turning away from it because some boxes will simply never be accessible.
